name: Nearby Ksour
hero_subtitle: Earthen fortified villages on the roads around Erfoud — Tafilalet architecture in its home landscape.

overview.title: Clay walls of the Tafilalet
overview.p1: Ksour and kasbah-style houses mark the Tafilalet as clearly as palms do. Around Erfoud, short detours reveal earthen walls, tower corners and lanes built for shade.
overview.p2: These are lived-in or semi-abandoned structures — not always ticketed monuments. A respectful exterior walk is often the right approach.
overview.p3: Soft morning or late light makes the clay glow; midday flattens detail and the heat is sharp.

1.title: Cooler
1.desc: Best for walking markets and photos.

food.title: Nearby food
food.p1: Simple tagines and cafés in Erfoud.

1.title: Access
1.desc: Best with a driver who knows which villages welcome visitors. Not every ksar is set up for tourism.

2.title: Respect
2.desc: These can be homes. Stay on public paths, dress modestly, ask before entering.

3.title: In a wider plan
3.desc: A ksar stop pairs well with the palm edges and a return to Erfoud for the night.

gyg.title: From Erfoud
gyg.subtitle: Desert day trips use desert roads.

q1.question: Is this the same as Rissani?
q1.answer: No. Rissani is a separate market town further south. These are villages reached from Erfoud itself.

q2.question: Do I need a guide?
q2.answer: Useful for context and access; not always mandatory for exterior views.

q3.question: How long?
q3.answer: One to two hours including transfer from town.

q4.question: Suitable for children?
q4.answer: Yes for a short exterior walk if heat is managed.

q5.question: Best photo light?
q5.answer: Early morning or late afternoon when the clay walls take on warm colour.
